title: Tor bounds over a constant field sheaf
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme and let $\kappa$ be a field [def-weil-field]. On a small representative of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in a universe containing the site, let $\kappa_X$ be the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use the abelian category of $\kappa_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\kappa)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and the ordinary K-flat derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For every $B\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\kappa)$ and every pair of integers $a\le b$, the following are equivalent:
$$
H^i(B)=0\quad(i\notin[a,b]),\qquad
H^i(B\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\kappa_X}N)=0\quad(i\notin[a,b])\text{ for every }\kappa_X\text{-module sheaf }N.
$$
In the second condition $N$ is placed in degree zero. Equivalently, $B$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] exactly when its cohomology is concentrated in that interval. Thus finite Tor amplitude is equivalent to bounded cohomology. No constructibility, Noetherianity, finiteness of $\kappa$, or existence of enough points is assumed.

source.place: First paragraph, residue-field finite Tor dimension calculation; expanded using the cited flatness and truncation statements.

external.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat)

proof.text: On the coefficient-sized small pro-etale site put R = kappa_X and A = Mod(R). Every module sheaf M is flat by lem-exc-constant-field-module-flat. Via the natural comparison siteSheafTensorRightIso, the monoidal functor tensorRight M is exact. Hence it preserves cohomology by lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology.

Assume H^i(B) vanishes outside [a,b]. Take any K-flat P with Q(P) isomorphic to B and any module sheaf M. The localization cohomology comparison homologyFunctorFactors identifies H^i(P) with H^i(B). CochainComplex.mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso identifies the total tensor P tensor M[0] with the complex obtained by applying tensorRight M termwise. Exactness from step 1 identifies its degree-i cohomology with H^i(P) tensor M, which is zero outside [a,b]. This verifies every representative and every module in HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude, with the original endpoints. K-flatness of P is not needed in this implication.

Conversely choose an arbitrary representing complex L for B using essential surjectivity of Q, and a K-flat quasi-isomorphism P -> L by lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Then Q(P) is isomorphic to B. Test the Tor predicate with this representative and the coefficient module R. The canonical ringedKoszulRightUnitIso identifies the total tensor P tensor R[0] with P. Applying cohomology to this unit isomorphism and the derived cohomology comparison gives the required vanishing of H^i(B). No boundedness assumption is used to choose the resolution.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); paragraph following Definition 08FZ (definition-tor-amplitude), testing with the coefficient module.

proof.text: Take existence of the same ordered integer endpoints in the two implications to obtain finite Tor amplitude if and only if bounded cohomology. In the reverse direction of this finite equivalence use the supplied inequality a <= b; in the forward direction it is part of the Tor predicate. Zero objects, singleton intervals and the empty site need no separate cases.

proof_origin.place: First paragraph, residue-field Tor bounds; shortened by exactness of tensoring with any constant-field module and the degree-zero tensor comparison. Exactness and unit test are from Stacks 03ER, 010N and 08FZ.

tool_uses.why: General constant-field sheaf flatness supplies flat terms on any small ringed site, without enough points; the unit has no other such node.
General site-level bounded-above flat K-flatness makes N[0] K-flat for every module N over the constant field, without topological-space or stalk hypotheses.
General ringed-site K-flat resolution of an arbitrary representative is used to verify tensor with the coefficient unit in the converse before boundedness is known.

General ringed-site fact (Stacks 06YP) that tensoring with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms; it transports the derived tensor from the defining resolution to the bounded representative, which is only isomorphic to B in D. No node of the unit gives it.

Step 3 cites lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent (Stacks 06YP), so Tot(−⊗N[0]) preserves quasi-isomorphisms and descends to D; this gives Q T_N(P')≅Q T_N(C)≅Q T_N(P), then the original degree count. proof_deps recomputed. lean.statement: theorem constant_field_tor_bounds (X : Scheme.{u}) (κ : Type (max v (u + 1))) [Field κ] (B : ConstantCompletion.D (ConstantCompletion.constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) κ)) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b) : (∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero ((coefficientModelCohomology (ConstantCompletion.constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) κ) i).obj B)) ↔ HasCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude X κ B a b
